checked_sources: Schur orthogonality and standard SU(2) quaternionic representation geometry
correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the exact hypothesis G≤SU(2) finite nonabelian, defining irreducible two-dimensional unitary block, nonzero u,v and rank-weighted transform normalization. Schur orthogonality puts only a nonzero rank-one defining block in Fourier space, giving sigma=2. SU(2)≅S³ unit quaternions and complex orthogonality identify coefficient zero equations with real two-planes P=a C_J; conversely every such plane occurs. Their intersections with G are empty or left cosets g(G∩U_J), finite cyclic; order two yields one antipodal pair, order>2 yields a maximal noncentral cyclic axis. To prove exactly two coefficient rays for a fixed coset, diagonalize a noncentral h in C: two independent complex vanish constraints annihilate A11,A22, rank(A)=1 forces off-diagonal product bc=0, hence E12 or E21 and no other rays. For an antipodal pair, the nondegenerate rank-one hyperplane section is a projective conic with finitely many extra-zero incidences; generic coefficients have none. Finite-axis arithmetic: 2T {4:3,6:4}, 2O {4:6,6:4,8:3}, 2I {4:15,6:10,10:6}, dicyclic one order-2n axis and n order-4 axes, yielding all displayed 2T/2O/2I/Dic_n zero-set and projective-ray counts. Recomputed Git tree SHA exactly and checked all 7 blob hashes against main. Independently enumerated real rank-two flats of all 24,48,120 exceptional unit-quaternion vectors by exact integer/quadratic-field arithmetic: {2:18,3:16}, {2:72,3:32,4:18}, {2:450,3:200,5:72}. Independently enumerated maximal cyclic subgroups and cosets for Dic_n n=2..20; all predictions matched. Infinite claim is proved by quaternionic plane and abstract group argument, not by finite enumeration.
residual_risks: Nonzero-vector and subgroup hypotheses are essential; not a statement about all Fourier-rank-two functions or arbitrary irreducible blocks.
Enumerations for Dic_n only n≤20: the general infinite formula relies on the proven standard dicyclic presentation, not computational extrapolation.
The exactly two rays are projective functions modulo nonzero complex scaling; counting nonprojective coefficients would give continuous fibres.
The geometry-to-coefficient implication assumes a faithful defining representation conjugate to standard SU(2), as specified.

value.rationale: A complete nonabelian Fourier support-set diagram for a canonical two-dimensional spin representation is mathematically motivated by the large gap between the general support-product uncertainty inequality and the actual allowed coefficient zeros. Beyond known subgroup and H4 flat counts, the classification uniquely specifies which cyclic cosets can occur as zero sets of a rank-one coefficient, proves converse realization in every binary polyhedral family, and separates finite identifiable two-ray projective fibres from infinite fibres for antipodal pairs. This structural identifiability boundary is useful to researchers reconstructing coefficients or classifying sharp noncommutative support constraints. The exact 2I table alone is covered prior art and is not counted as the standalone contribution; small finite cases are not the primary source of value.
residual_risks: The application is narrow: only rank-one defining spin coefficients, not all Fourier-rank-two functions, and no new sharp uncertainty inequality for arbitrary blocks.

Projective fibre geometry is elementary once spinor-Grassmann duality is recognized; value lies in the combined complete classification and interpretation, not in claiming a novel general Grassmannian principle.

final_claim: For every nonabelian finite G⊂SU(2), every nonzero rank-one defining-spin matrix coefficient has weighted Fourier support exactly 2, and its zero set is empty, an antipodal pair, or a coset of a maximal cyclic subgroup of order>2. Every such set is realized. Every coset has exactly two projective coefficient rays; pair zero sets have infinite projective fibres. Complete incidence counts: Dic_n n≥2 total n²+2n+3 (size2:2n, size4:n², size2n:2, empty:1), 2T 47 (2:12,4:18,6:16,empty:1), 2O 147 (2:24,4:72,6:32,8:18,empty:1), 2I 783 (2:60,4:450,6:200,10:72,empty:1); 2(n²+2),68,244,1444 projective rigid rays respectively. For Dic_2 repeated size4 categories combine into six distinct size4 sets.
limitations: All finite nonabelian G≤SU(2) are within scope; cyclic groups, other irreducibles, arbitrary rank-two block functions and coefficient matrices of rank two are outside.
The numerical 2I H4 flat multiplicities are published in Bao et al. 2010 and explicitly not a new enumeration; other classification inputs are standard.
Projective fibre multiplicity means modulo nonzero complex scalar, not number of actual nonprojective functions.
Finite exact tests are corroboration, not proof for all n; the infinite dicyclic and all-coefficient claims rely on the analytic quaternionic-group argument.
Bounded prior-art comparison cannot rule out older spinor/Segre root-matroid equivalent formulations; no external expert attestation or Lean formalization claimed.
